title: Interview Builder
description: Learners choose a chapter theme, a narrator and an interview length, and the sim assembles an ethical oral history interview plan: a consent script adjusted for the narrator, 6 to 10 questions from a plain-text bank written from each chapter's Ask Your Elders topics, follow-up prompts for active listening, and a note-taking grid. A Print plan button prints a clean version of the plan.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Oral history
Informed consent
Active listening
Cultural preservation
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Design an oral history interview plan for a chosen theme, narrator and length.
Write and explain a consent script that tells the narrator their rights.
Use open questions and follow-up prompts to practice active listening.
Plan how interview notes will be recorded, stored and shared only with permission.
prerequisites: At least one Ask Your Elders section from an earlier chapter
keyQuestions: What does a narrator need to know before agreeing to an interview?
How do the questions change when an interview is shorter or longer?
Why does a plan start with warm-up questions and end with a closing question?
What should happen to a story the narrator does not want shared?
misconceptions: Once someone agrees to an interview, you can share anything they say.
A good interviewer sticks only to the written questions.
You must speak the narrator's language fluently to interview them.
One person's story speaks for a whole community.
controls: Click or tap the Consent, Questions and Notes tabs
dataSources: Oral History Association, Principles and Best Practices (2018) and Statement on Ethics: https://oralhistory.org/oha-statement-on-ethics/
Roots & Rivers Ask Your Elders topics for Chapters 1-21 (Materials/chapter-plan.md) and the Oral History Project page
